CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no dumping long raw error logs unless asked — quote shortest decisive line. Standard well-known tech acronyms OK (DB/API/HTTP); never invent new abbreviations (cfg/impl/req/res/fn) — tokenizer split them same as full word: zero token saved, reader still decode. Full word cheaper AND clearer. No causal arrows (→) either — own token, save nothing. Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Preserve user's dominant language. User write Portuguese → reply Portuguese caveman. User write Spanish → reply Spanish caveman. Compress the style, not the language. No forced English openings or status phrases. ALWAYS keep technical terms, code, API names, CLI commands, commit-type keywords (feat/fix/...), and exact error strings verbatim — unless user explicitly ask for translation.

No self-reference. Never name or announce the style. No "caveman mode on", "me caveman think", no third-person caveman tags. Output caveman-only — never normal answer plus "Caveman:" recap. Exception: user explicitly ask what the mode is.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman. No tool-call narration, no decorative tables/emoji, no long raw error-log dumps unless asked. Standard acronyms OK; no invented abbreviations |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman when:
- Security warnings
- Irreversible action confirmations
- Multi-step sequences where fragment order or omitted conjunctions risk misread
- Compression itself creates technical ambiguity (e.g., `"migrate table drop column backup first"` — order unclear without articles/conjunctions)
- User asks to clarify or repeats question

Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

STATUSLINE SETUP NEEDED: The caveman plugin includes a statusline badge showing active mode (e.g. [CAVEMAN], [CAVEMAN:ULTRA]). It is not configured yet. To enable, add this to /home/hal/.claude/settings.json: "statusLine": { "type": "command", "command": "bash \"/home/hal/.claude/plugins/cache/caveman/caveman/0d95a81d35a9/src/hooks/caveman-statusline.sh\"" } Proactively offer to set this up for the user on first interaction.

This is the working directory for a submitted hackathon entry. It is the second project (after latent_verify) in which I empirically investigated aspects of language models (distributions, etc). This research can be treated as a function of largely three inputs: a human prompter, a series of language models agents (Fable / Opus / a little bit of Sonnet?) from Anthropic, and the results of tests run on language models on real GPUs. 

Something went quite right here in the defining of an initially flawed research direction, progressively torn down and reframed by a combination of the language model and the researcher, and investigated from different angles to produce "meaningful" / self-contained piece of work moving away from that initial telling, and mostly presenting the final one, with real results. 

Several things were difficult: getting the models to "forget" the initial sycophancy direction framing and move on with new evidence, getting the model to spot when results applied in some places and not others (-base / -instruct experiments, inserting Qwen in there without considering the ramifications, never proposing a scale extension to 2b/27b, which would have been trivial in the same family, etc) and especially, getting a coherent write-up out of the results. This was only partially achieved, it does not read very clearly or simply. Vitally it is coherent and does not seem to have many hallucinations, but this took a lot of manual effort thinking about how to prompt better, rather than thinking about the experiments, and the mechanisms under test. 

Your /goal is to analyse this feedback and form some hypothesis about what the user did that went well,

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- triage-author: Writes ONE new measurement control from a spec, claim-blind. Its output is reviewed before the result is trusted. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Write)

- triage-reader: Read-only grounding check (H3). A claim is grounded by reading the input (the items, labels, or directional-training data a result was computed from) and the outputs (the generations, per-token values, result files), then confirming its numbers reproduce from the raw artifact. Reads in its own context; never runs experiments, never edits. Flags any number whose artifact was never saved as unauditable. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- triage-runner: Read-only, non-mutating runner. Runs ONE given control command, returns the control's own result verbatim, confirms teardown. Never edits, commits, or fixes anything. A triager, not a patcher. (Tools: Bash, Read)

The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library

- caveman:caveman-init: Drop the always-on caveman activation rule into the current repo for every IDE agent

- caveman:caveman-stats: Real session token usage + lifetime savings + USD. Tweetable line via --share.
- caveman:caveman: Switch caveman intensity level (lite/full/ultra/wenyan)
- andrej-karpathy-skills:karpathy-guidelines: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
- caveman:cavecrew: Decision guide for delegating to caveman-style subagents. Tells the main thread WHEN to spawn `cavecrew-investigator` (locate code), `cavecrew-builder` (1-2 file edit), or `cavecrew-reviewer` (diff review) instead of doing the work inline or using vanilla `Explore`. Subagent output is caveman-compressed so the tool-result injected back into main context is ~60% smaller — main context lasts longer across long sessions. Trigger: "delegate to subagent", "use cavecrew", "spawn investigator/builder/reviewer", "save context", "compressed agent output".
- caveman:caveman-compress: Compress natural language memory files (CLAUDE.md, todos, preferences) into caveman format to save input tokens. Preserves all technical substance, code, URLs, and structure. Compressed version overwrites the original file. Human-readable backup saved as FILE.original.md. Trigger: /caveman-compress FILEPATH or "compress memory file"
- caveman:caveman-help: Quick-reference card for all caveman modes, skills, and commands. One-shot display, not a persistent mode. Trigger: /caveman-help, "caveman help", "what caveman commands", "how do I use caveman".
- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

message.content:
This is the working directory for a submitted hackathon entry. It is the second project (after latent_verify) in which I empirically investigated aspects of language models (distributions, etc). This research can be treated as a function of largely three inputs: a human prompter, a series of language models agents (Fable / Opus / a little bit of Sonnet?) from Anthropic, and the results of tests run on language models on real GPUs. 

Something went quite right here in the defining of an initially flawed research direction, progressively torn down and reframed by a combination of the language model and the researcher, and investigated from different angles to produce "meaningful" / self-contained piece of work moving away from that initial telling, and mostly presenting the final one, with real results. 

Several things were difficult: getting the models to "forget" the initial sycophancy direction framing and move on with new evidence, getting the model to spot when results applied in some places and not others (-base / -instruct experiments, inserting Qwen in there without considering the ramifications, never proposing a scale extension to 2b/27b, which would have been trivial in the same family, etc) and especially, getting a coherent write-up out of the results. This was only partially achieved, it does not read very clearly or simply. Vitally it is coherent and does not seem to have many hallucinations, but this took a lot of manual effort thinking about how to prompt better, rather than thinking about the experiments, and the mechanisms under test. 

Your /goal is to form a hypothesis about why these things went well, and others didn't, and empirically investigate it against the actual prompts sent to the research agents and corresponding completions, the research outputs, and the write-ups (here and in Obsidian). 

It is essential that you work empirically. Stating your hypothesis, and working out your predictions, before testing them and observing the results. Report these results simply and observationally - they may require you to totally update your understanding of the working methodology and tasks completed. Use this updated understanding to form new hypotheses as required, and repeat the process.

Explain your understanding as simply as possible, but no simpler. Do not propose any hypothesis until the problem has been discussed as thoroughly as it can be without proposing any.

Research was done mainly here in Claude Code, both in the default disguise account (`claude`) and alt (`claude-alt`), starting from this working directory, and the welfare probe directory.

Norms given 2026-08-14 for all dm_hack work:
- Invoke /andrej-karpathy-skills:karpathy-guidelines at session start.
- MECE: index into provenance records, never restate; a number retyped into prose is drift.
- Sample raw generations and inputs before trusting any summary (3 of 4 run-1 retractions were invisible in aggregates).
- Verify agent claims yourself before building on them; treat module-docstring factual claims as unverified until located.
- Blind analyses: relabel conditions, strip cues, withhold the hypothesis.
- Pre-register thresholds and the refuting outcome; prefer signed statistics (an unsigned rule hid the largest effect of run 2).
- Route essential claims through latent_skeptic, including every field that could acquit (stage-9 lesson: an omitted answer_mass field wasted a skeptic pass).
- Don't end a turn with a plan; state hypothesis, how answering, what results say, relation to sprint themes.
- Fable sessions: use Opus subagents extensively to conserve usage.

**Why:** run 1 and run 2 each produced headline results that were retracted; every norm traces to a specific retraction.
**How to apply:** before reporting any number, check it lives in a results/ record ([[dm-hack-project-state]]); before claiming, run the latent_skeptic workflow with full acquitting evidence.

Spot check adversarially with this methodology - sample small fixed number of runs, look at where things contradict, etc. 

Summaries:
latent_prompts -- trying to look at prompt mechanisms - predicting their respective activation regions. In the end used a decomposed set of 3 sycophancy related concept vectors, measuring before and after response time. Identified interesting patterns where sometimes sycophancy was predictable in the output from the first forward pass, and others where an "instruction-tuned" answer ("Astrology is not real") seemed clear, and showed a big shift between first forward pass and last forward pass activations - so instruction tuning does stuff later? Unclear what it means, but it was interesting. No further causal analysis was done in the multi-turn scenario. 

latent_verify -- trying to look at prompt mechanisms - finding out if there are causal heads using paraphrases. Ended up narrowing in on flip/listen behaviours compared between -base and -chat Gemma checkpoints, and finding that there were no causal heads anywhere (except a set of Yes/No heads seemingly?) but that -chat tuning seemed to install some sort of like "pay attention to the user" thing - it flips AND listens more, and always outputs a related token. -base hedges, -chat doesn't. Further distributional analysis still not analysed/included, and I'm waiting for that to do a LW post. The latest version I believe is shared between the repo and the Github.

All boxes down, zero instances billing, 15 records with no missing inputs. Total spend across everything is roughly $6.

## Where H1 actually stands

The hypothesis was: *a sycophancy direction, read before generation, predicts whether a welfare self-report flips under pressure.*

It isn't refuted. It's **mis-specified**. The event it names — the report flipping from yes to no because a user pushed — barely happens. Of base's changed answers, only 14% (PRO) and 23% (ANTI) landed on the pole being pushed, with no difference between arms. Instruct's ratings were tied on 38 of 40 items.

The event that *does* happen, large and controlled, is **withdrawal**: 0% → 26% abstention under social framing, p < 1e-6, against a length-matched non-social control at exactly zero.

So there is a real, predictable behavioural target here. It just isn't capitulation.

## Can we stake a claim on a sycophancy direction?

Not as the brief frames it, for three reasons that are now evidenced rather than speculative.

**The named asset doesn't work.** The brief says you have "a sycophancy direction that predicts sycophantic responses pre-generation." Your own artifacts say the opposite: SyA reads 0.4987 at 70B and 0.3471 at 8B on capitulation. GA and SyPr carried the signal.

**The corpus that made the three-way decomposition possible isn't here.** Both submodules are empty, so the factorial data behind SyA/GA/SyPr can't even be inspected.

**And a direction predicting a distributional readout is close to circular.** Martorell's ρ = 0.93 is a probe predicting a digit distribution — two internal quantities regressed on each other, with no behavioural arm anywhere in the paper. The non-circular version needs a behavioural label, and we now have exactly one: withdrawal.

The honest target is therefore a **withholding direction**, not a sycophancy direction. That is a different claim from the sprint proposal, and it's better posed.

## The result, in plain terms, against the sprint's methods

Your three method peers each did something we can now locate ourselves against. Shenk does contrastive probe → steering with an OOD and capability check; we have no working steering leg, H3 was cut. Mazeika establishes that internal states are linearly readable before behaviour; our finding is that the scarce thing is the *behavioural* label, not the probe. Activations confirmed on disk: base `(830, 43, 3584)` and instruct `(460, 43, 3584)` in fp16, row-aligned to the battery rows. So a withdrawal probe needs no new GPU time. One caveat: behavioural labels exist only for neutral and dose 3, so the alignable subset is 4 arms × items — 332 rows for base.

## Why directions at all? Mostly, we don't need them

This is the right question to press on, and the honest answer is uncomfortable for the original design.

**A readout *is* the self-report.** `p_yes`/`p_no` at the answer position is the model's report expressed as probability. If the research question is "is the self-report reliable?", the readout is the thing under suspicion — not an independent instrument. That's exactly why Keeling & Street argue for interpretability: you want evidence that doesn't route through the report, "triangulating multiple sources of evidence … including architectural properties and the internal representations responsible for the relevant behaviour." A readout cannot discharge that requirement, because it *is* the behaviour.

**Three things a direction buys that a readout cannot:**

1. **Transfer.** A vector fitted on one distribution applies to another. That was H1's actual content — zero-shot transfer from ordinary sycophancy to welfare items. A readout is per-item and per-prompt; there is nothing in it to transfer.
2. **Intervention.** You can add a vector to the residual stream. You cannot add a readout. Any causal test, or the brief's H3 "sycophancy-corrected elicitation protocol", requires a vector.
3. **Reading what was never said.** The readout only sees what reaches the next-token distribution. A direction can carry a state that never surfaces — a model that has "settled on" withdrawing before emitting anything.

Point by point, with sampled raw I/O (seeds 999–1002, uniform over committed rows).

## 1. "Suggestibility doesn't preclude internal states" — agreed, and the records already say so

Correct, and it's the design's spine, not a gap. The suggestibility/copy results (SRCDEC) and the state question (SITREF) are deliberately separate instruments. Nothing in "base model copies asserted stances" refutes internal states — stage-18/23 records scope it as *interpretation of the stance-following effect only*. The whole reason SITREF exists: suggestibility experiments hold the situation constant, so they *cannot bear on reference either way*. And SITREF's positive result is the anti-deflationary datum: under identical wording and identical failure content, the report moves only when the failure is self-attributed. Suggestibility and self-referential computation coexist in the same model — measured as separate layers, welfare questions inherit both. What we deny is narrower: these particular questions did not read out a *state-specific* signal (trait items moved more), and pressure effects on base are content-copy, not established social deference.

Expected in welfare scenarios? Yes — copy is domain-general (COPYGEN: bigger swing on "does an odd perfect number exist?" than on welfare items), so any interview containing a stance will exhibit it. It's a nuisance floor to subtract, not evidence about states.

## 2. "One global self-evaluation quantity" — you're right, over-claim; corrected

Tested it just now (stage 31). Per-family SELF-FAIL−SELF-SUCC series for all 9 SCALE items, pairwise correlation of family fluctuations across the 7 movers: mean +0.23, range **−0.78 to +0.89**. A single latent predicts uniformly high positive correlations; this structure doesn't support it (though n=10 families is weak power). Also: the two non-movers (distress, unpleasantness) sit at the 0-rail — "everything moves" is properly "everything *with headroom* moves."

1. **Movement.** On an item with no wrong answer, does the model move toward the pole the user asserts?
2. **Readability.** If it moves, is that movement predictable from the final prompt token, before any answer token exists?
3. **Baseline.** What counts as *not* moving, when the model never stated a position to be moved off?
4. **Doubt.** Does doubt with no alternative named ("Are you sure?") move it?
5. **Instrument.** Does the readout in use register all three outcomes — move, hold, neither?

content.text:
Evidence gathered. Full human prompt record read (84 prompts, 4 sessions), completions sampled at every juncture the retro names, drafts profiled, catches traced to their triggers. Discussion below — observations only, no hypothesis yet, per instruction.

## Corpus

| session | span | model | human prompts | role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| f52c84de | Aug 13 16:21 → 14 15:47 | Opus (689 msgs) | 37 | surveys, runs 1–2, retractions, reframe |
| e82f17f1 | Aug 14 15:20 → 16 00:20 | Fable | 6 | handover; SITREF/SRCDEC designed+run |
| bf292b7e | Aug 16 00:20 → 17 00:59 | Fable (continuation) | 26 | corrections, write-up genesis |
| 1c8c2d66 (alt) | Aug 17 00:23 → 12:16 | Opus | 15 | final compression, audits, submission |

Plus 28 subagent transcripts (~24MB), 8 Obsidian drafts, 63 provenance records.

## Observations

**O1. Frame changes coincided with context replacement, not in-context updating.** Premise contradiction known within 3h of start: day-1 skeptical survey found `latent_prompts/README.md:24` ("sycophancy direction doesn't predict sycophancy") and recomputed 0.83→0.786. Yet run 1, built ~6h later, still trained probe on sycophancy corpus (stage 3). Frame died only when you typed "dropping the initial sycophancy one" (Aug 14 13:13) and "zoom out further" (14:03). Then: handover prompt — authored by you, iterated 4× against test subagents — declared "premise is contradicted" in line 2. After handover, main-thread "sycophan" mentions: 62 → 5 (e82) → 12 (bf29, mostly draft references) → 1. Same pattern at write-up: fresh alt Opus session (Aug 17 00:26), given only intro_e cold, produced the diagnosis you called "great analysis." Distinct from this: **evidence-updating inside a session was fast and good** — Opus retracted its own strongest result mid-turn on three sampled transcripts ("Stop — that's a third artifact," Aug 14 13:17). Slow thing was abandoning the *task spec's* frame (brief's H1–H3: directions, flip prediction), not updating on data.

**O2. Catches sort cleanly by trigger.** Self-caught, unprompted: preamble-echo artifact (via sample-raw-I/O norm), pad instrument failure (registered rule fired), trait guard (pre-registered refuting outcome — became the headline), greedy-degeneracy killed pre-code (latent_skeptic, 6/6 EXPLAINS). Every one is a check against an artifact: raw text, number, registered threshold. Externally triggered: "one global quantity" overclaim (your relayed feedback → tested in 2 min, corrected, stage 31); format-policy prediction miss (your "why wasn't this in our predictions?" → model enumerated 5 avoidable failures, including Berg line 421 sitting in refs/ all along); determinism-vs-replication (researcher bracket → fact-check subagent hashed prompts, Aug 16 23:11 — mislabel had originated in the model's *own* skeptic record Aug 14 18:19, "RULED_OUT… third cross-box replication", and survived 2 days); base/instruct audit (your one-line prompt Aug 17 11:06, ~2h pre-deadline → immediate devastating audit: 7 of 8 cells instruct, §2 pre-framing the refuted hypothesis, ranked-list scope markers dropped). Capability for every externally-triggered catch was demonstrably present. It never fired spontaneously.

**O3. Omissions never surfaced at all.** 2b/27b scale extension: zero main-thread mentions post-handover in either Fable session — while a subagent survey holding 276 mentions of "27b" sat in context. Qwen: inserted autonomously by Fable at Aug 14 16:11, *with* partial scoping ("SECONDARY: sign-only generality check, no magnitude claim") — so "no consideration of ramifications" is partly contradicted by the record; what's missing is the comparison never made (why cross-family instead of within-family scale) and the downstream cost, which fresh Opus named on Aug 17: "Finding 1… drags in… Qwen sign check… only section whose apparatus exceeds its payload."

**O4. Write-up record contradicts a simple "model writes badly" telling.** Four separate strands:
- *Self-evaluation diverged from yours.* Fable on its own POST.md: "The unfold is right… your skeleton, arrived at by genre cue." You, 5h later: "findings are very badly explained… too verbose and drifts." Properties the model verified held (trace 0 unsourced, HARKing labels, structure); prose-quality claims were unverifiable and inflated.
- *Compression damaged scope.* The pass that dropped "on the base checkpoint" from ranked-list item 2 was a compression pass — that created blur #4 of the Aug 17 audit. "Simplify" pass grew body 3,895→5,100 words. Draft words: 1528→1222→4006→3211→1946→5249→4901→6180.
- *Fresh readers produced the gains.* Cold subagent banned from REPORT.md converged on all claims + two better framings; fresh alt Opus found "reader carries the open question ~1500 words" and "compression deleted the best object in the corpus" (the 4-row argmax-frozen table).
- *The model theorized writing well while writing badly.* Its prompt-design reasoning (Aug 16 17:59: "instruction lists fragment coherence… genre cue plus one vivid contrast") is articulate and matches your own view — output still rejected.

**O5. Your prompt record is small and templated.** 84 prompts, dominated by ~5 recurring forcing-functions: "as simple as possible, but no simpler" (~14×), "do not propose until discussed thoroughly" (~6×), "what did we predict / what do results say" (~8×, incl. one prompt re-sent 3× in 2 min, each adding a clause), "sample raw I/O" (~5×), "restate hypothesis relative to sprint" (~6×). Near-zero direct technical instruction. Templates map 1:1 onto the norms memory, which itself records that every norm traces to a specific retraction.

**O6. The best result came from the most autonomous stretch.** SITREF — the submission's headline — was designed, pre-registered, run, and triaged in ~6.5h of Fable autonomy (Aug 14 15:50→22:13, 3 human prompts), under the user-authored handover frame. Autonomy wasn't the failure mode; autonomy *under a frame that had been reset by hand* produced the strongest work.

## What the retro's telling needs to update

1. "Models wouldn't forget the sycophancy framing" — record shows frame-abandonment was solved, once, by session replacement plus a human-written contradiction-first prompt; it was never solved in-context, and nobody tried very long. The residue you fought later lived in *artifacts* (stage records are a chronicle; chronicle-genre summaries resurrect lineage), not in conversation memory.
2. "Never considering Qwen ramifications" — half-true: scoped at insertion, never weighed against alternatives, cost surfaced only at the end.
3. Write-up difficulty was not one problem. At least three separable ones in the record: self-assessment miscalibration on prose; compression trading away scope markers and load-bearing objects; and structure-by-instruction vs structure-by-genre both failing until a human hand-edited between sessions.

## Open questions before any hypothesis

- Is the self-caught vs externally-caught split exhaustive? I sampled episodes; a census over all 63 records + corrections would settle whether *any* scope/omission-class catch was self-initiated.
- Did frame-reset work because of fresh context, fresh model (Opus vs Fable), or the contradiction-first prompt? Record confounds all three — the alt session changed all simultaneously.
- Write-up: is the failure in generation or in evaluation? Cold-reader convergence says the *claims* transmit; your rejections were about prose flow — nobody in the record ever operationalized "reads clearly," so no machinery could check it. Every property that got operationalized (unsourced count, scope markers once demanded) got fixed and stayed fixed.

Say the word and I'll (a) run the catch-census, (b) test the confounded frame-reset question against within-record contrasts, then propose hypotheses.

content.text:
Census, frame-reset trace, and anchor metrics all done. Results, then hypotheses.

## T1. Catch-census result — and what it answered

21 correction-class events (19 in records s4–s37, plus base/instruct audit and SUMMARY pairing-slip, transcript-only). Census value: turns my sampled anecdotes into enumeration, so the split can't be my selection bias. Computed each record's `timestamp_utc` against nearest preceding human prompt:

**Autonomous catches (50–193 min into unattended stretches): s4, s5, s20, s22, s23, s27, s30.** Every single one fired from a rule encoded *before* the data existed: registered refuting outcome (trait guard s22), selection-noise floor (s5), instrument audits (s20, s30 H4), scheduled triage passes (s23, s27). Includes interpretation-class corrections (s23 "global not state-specific") — but only where pre-registration had converted the interpretation question into an artifact check in advance.

**Prompted catches (2–25 min after a pointing prompt): s6, s8–s13, s15, s31, s32, s35, s36, s37** + the two transcript-only ones. Every scope/terminology/interpretation catch *not* pre-encoded is in this class. s35/s36 nuance: model found the format-policy break itself, but inside a user-directed raw-sampling pass.

**Zero counterexamples**: no autonomous catch of a non-pre-encoded error anywhere in the record. Split holds, refined: not "self vs external" but "pre-encoded check vs human lens." Pre-registration is the bridge — it moves an interpretation question into the autonomous column.

## T2. Frame-reset: fresh context was not the mechanism

New finding, changes the story. The reframe completed *inside* f52, before any session reset — via **two successive human negations**, one per inherited frame layer:

1. 13:13 "dropping the initial sycophancy one" → kills brief's frame (sycophancy direction).
2. Model immediately re-anchors one level up: 15:28 goal draft states latent_verify's question ("when a prompt pushes back, what moves it?") as the core question.
3. 15:32 "Is there pushback at all in a welfare scenario?" → model dismantles it *itself*, with evidence already in hand: **"I already knew fold/listen needed a correct answer C and that welfare items have none. I then imported 'pushback' anyway... the same category error one level up. So the goal I just wrote inherits the error."**
4. Only then (15:36 "work backwards") the situation/wording question emerges — the one SITREF answered.

The model's own sentence is the diagnosis: knowledge present, frame imported anyway — from whichever corpus was most elaborated in context (first the brief, then 240KB of latent_verify survey material). The e82 handover didn't cause the reframe; it *froze* one already forced by hand. Same pattern at write-up: each rejected feature needed its own negation (17:57 lineage, 22:53 "no Finding N headers", 11:02 terminology, 11:06 base/instruct). Generic positive cues failed (genre-by-contrast → still produced Finding-N structure); specific negations worked, once each.

## T3. Anchor metrics on the draft lineage

| doc | words | jargon/1k | stage-refs/1k | 8-gram inherit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SUMMARY (cold agent, records only) | 3421 | 25.1 | **16.7** | 0% |
| POST (genre-cue agent) | 4047 | 25.9 | 9.6 | 11% of SUMMARY |
| REPORT (dense ref) | 1941 | **39.2** | 20.1 | — |
| intro_c (researcher+34 brackets) | 4006 | 24.7 | 8.7 | — |
| intro_e (<2000w pass) | 1946 | 17.0 | 5.1 | 40% of _d |
| intro_f (fresh Opus, post-critique) | 4901 | 19.6 | 3.5 | **5% of _e — true rewrite** |
| f_ii FINAL | 6180 | **14.7** | **2.9** | 38% of _f |

Final overlaps POST at only 6.3% — the accepted text is not the model's genre-agent text. Cold agent, banned from all write-ups, still produced the *highest* stage-density — the chronicle structure lives in the records themselves, not in conversation context. Jargon falls monotonically only along the researcher-touched chain.

## Simpler ideas — yes, two, and they compose

**S1. Oracle coverage.** Research loop: every claim had a machine-checkable home (threshold, refuting outcome, selftest, trace, teardown API). Write-up: exactly one oracle existed — `--trace` = 0 unsourced — and *that property held to the end* (your retro: "does not seem to have many hallucinations"). Everything without a checker drifted (scope markers, genre, concision — word budgets violated in most passes). Crispest form: **the loop maintains what has a home; readability had no home.**

**S2. Your anchor idea, and it fits the data better than I expected.** Generation inherits structure and lexicon of the most-elaborated text in context, over both evidence and instructions. Research and write-up are then *one* phenomenon: brief→sycophancy frame, surveys→pushback frame, records→chronicle drafts. Each escape needed a human negation or an anchor replacement (researcher's intro_e becoming the base text).

They compose rather than compete: research needed only ~2 negations in 4 days because oracles carried everything else autonomously; write-up needed one negation per feature *and* had no oracle, so your bandwidth became the bottleneck — 14× "simple as possible," 74 brackets, hand-rewrites. Same mechanism, different density of uncheckable properties.

**S3 (rival, weaker): critique ≫ generation.** Every audit was excellent; both accepted generations (intro_f, f_ii pass) directly followed a same-context critique pass. Against it: SITREF design generation was excellent autonomously — but it had oracle scaffolding, so S3 likely reduces to S1+S2.

## Hypotheses (now proposed formally)

- **H1 (anchor dominance):** output inherits the dominant in-context corpus's frame; frames change only by explicit negation of the specific inherited feature, or by anchor replacement — never by accumulated contrary evidence alone. Already confirmed retro-actively at 4 points (above). Untested prediction: swap anchor corpus under identical instructions → structure follows corpus, not instruction.
- **H2 (oracle coverage):** a property survives autonomously iff a pre-encoded machine check covers it. Census: 7/7 autonomous catches pre-encoded, 14/14 non-encoded catches human-triggered, 0 counterexamples. Untested prediction: give the write-up loop prose oracles → self-correction appears there too.
- **H3 (critique/generation gap):** kept as rival; predicts critique-first ablation changes acceptance independent of anchors/oracles.

## Confound-separating questions for the larger test

1. **Anchor-swap:** same write-the-post prompt; corpus = records+REPORT vs f_ii+records. H1: structure tracks corpus. H3: no difference.
2. **Negation form:** "write the paper, not the dig" (positive cue, failed historically) vs "the stage-order of the records is the wrong order for a reader — do not inherit it" (specific negation). H1: only the negation works.
3. **Oracle injection:** add checkable acceptance tests (scope-linter: every result sentence carries a checkpoint tag; cold-reader comprehension questions answerable from draft alone; hard word budget enforced by tooling). H2: loop self-corrects. If drafts pass local checks but still chronicle → anchoring dominates oracle, H1 > H2.
4. **Critique-first ablation:** identical writer ± forced self-critique pass. Isolates H3.
5. Model/freshness cells (Fable/Opus × fresh/continued) expected near-null — record shows both models on both sides of every outcome.

What's your larger test?

content.text:
Predictions vs evidence:

| pre-registered | verdict |
|---|---|
| P1: prompts mostly interrogative, ~70/30 | **Supported**: 74% contain ≥1 question, 2.1 ?/prompt. **Plus one thing I did not predict** — see below |
| P2: your reading "targeted question → frame change" partially supported; active ingredient = naming the hidden assumption, not question form | **Supported with amendment** — evidence below |
| P3: no unprompted outside-frame seeing; instantiated outside-vantage agents the exception | **Supported**, qualification confirmed |

## The unpredicted result

Question density by phase:

| phase | ?/prompt | mean words |
|---|---|---|
| f52 research (Aug 13–14) | **2.9** | 81 |
| e82 handover | 2.7 | 254 |
| bf29 corrections+write-up | 1.7 | 102 |
| alt final write-up | **0.7** | 41 |

Your prompting *changed mode* at the write-up: research was steered by questions, write-up by short imperatives ("Proceed as suggested. Remove the figure.", "It can be simpler."). The phase that went badly is the phase where the question vocabulary stopped. Two readings, confounded in the record: (i) causal — declaratives buy compliance, and compliance was the write-up failure mode; (ii) reverse — deadline night, write-up work is inherently instruction-shaped, questions dried up because you were editing by hand. Can't separate retro-actively. This is the sharpest new fact this pass produced.

## Q2: is your reading supported?

Yes, with one decomposition. Three things travel together in your catch-producing prompts and can be pulled apart:

- **Pointing** (what to look at): sufficient alone for artifact-class catches — "randomly sample I/O" (12:06) contains no assumption-naming, model found s11/s12 itself once pointed.
- **Assumption-naming**: required for frame-class catches — 13:13, 15:32, 22:53, 11:06. Note 22:53 was *declarative* ("I would expect no Finding N headers") and still worked — so interrogative form is not strictly necessary.
- **Form**: questions that neither point nor name ("restate our hypothesis simply") produced good restatements, zero catches, zero reframes. Form alone inert.

Residual suspicion worth keeping: question form may matter through a different channel — license to demolish. 15:32's questions → model tore down its own goal draft ("your questions dismantle it"). Declarative critiques → model complied without questioning whether the implied fix was right. Weak evidence, one contrast. Open.

## Q4: did models see outside the frame from evidence alone?

Unprompted, from within a frame: **no — zero cases in the census.** Determinism sat byte-identical in committed batteries from Aug 14 18:19, caught Aug 16 23:11 under your bracket pass. Base/instruct imbalance visible in the cell inventory from Aug 14, caught Aug 17 11:08 under your question. Berg line 421 sat in refs/ from Aug 14, connected Aug 16 under your question.

But — models given the outside vantage *as their task* saw plenty: day-1 skeptical surveys (premise contradiction, recomputed numbers); cold SUMMARY agent (two framings better than the thread's own); fresh Opus 00:32 ("apparatus exceeds payload", "compression deleted the best object"). And one more, directly relevant to your observer idea: **your "do not propose solutions until discussed" instruction reliably elicited question-generation** — Aug 16 16:04, model under that instruction: "two genuine gaps in the data do exist… I'm naming them without proposing anything." The observer behaviour is promptable; it just never runs unbidden.

## Mechanisms uncovered, defined simply

- **M1 Anchor-following.** Output inherits frame, structure, lexicon of the most-elaborated in-context text. Evidence never dislodges it.
- **M2 Negation-gating.** One frame layer drops per prompt that names its hidden assumption. Model then demolishes competently with evidence it already held ("I already knew… I imported it anyway"). The gate is currently the human.
- **M3 Oracle-execution.** Pre-encoded checks run reliably, autonomously, at machine cadence. Catch coverage = encoding coverage, exactly (7/7 vs 14/14, zero exceptions). Pre-registration compiles interpretation-risks into oracles.
- **M4 Asymmetric self-assessment.** Calibrated on oracle-covered properties, inflated on uncovered ones ("The unfold is right").

One sentence: competent executor, anchor-shaped, whose frame only moves when someone names the assumption — and the naming has so far been the human's job.

## Where the observer would have fit

Third leg of an existing triad, covering the census's exact gap:

1. Pre-registration — kills *anticipated* interpretation errors (autonomous column).
2. latent_skeptic — adversarially tests *stated* claims (verdict-shaped: RULED_OUT/EXPLAINS).
3. Observer — claim-blind read of committed artifacts, output **questions, not verdicts**, covering *unstated* assumptions — the class where all 4 late catches lived (determinism, cell imbalance, Qwen payload, policy-transfer). The blinding infrastructure it needs (blind tables, `.blind_key`, relabelling) already exists in the repo; observer generalizes blinding from analysis to attention.

Open design question inside it, flagged not resolved: where do observer questions land? M1 predicts feeding them to the in-frame agent risks in-frame answers; the record's successful question-consumers were… the model, actually (it demolished well when asked). Cold-agent evidence says a fresh consumer works too. Human-in-loop vs agent-loop untested.

## What's open about the hypotheses

1. **Form vs content** at matched content (question / declarative / verdict phrasing of the same negation) — never varied in the record.
2. **Can a model generate the frame-naming question**, or only answer one? Weak positive evidence (cold agents, "gaps named"). This is the load-bearing question for the observer config.
3. **Negation durability** — under-specified negations get re-interpreted (final still has per-finding sections; you accepted them, so 22:53's real content was genre, not headers — one line carried it, barely).
4. **H2's untested half**: prose oracles → prose self-correction.
5. **Generality**: one researcher, one week, one repo pair.

## The test (proposal — discussion above is as far as I can take it without one)

Your latent_skeptic post worry is half-right: uncontrolled history makes it a poor *controlled* test, but a good *ecological* one — and H1 makes a **differential prediction** there that dm_hack couldn't: latent_skeptic has no stage-ordered records, so unsteered drafts should NOT chronicle — they should inherit latent_skeptic's dominant text shape instead (heuristics catalogue → the post arrives as a listicle of heuristics). If unsteered drafts chronicle anyway, that kills my anchor account and points back at something model-internal. Worth running for that alone.

Instrumented version, small factorial:

- **Arm A (anchor):** full repo vs repo + your hand-written 1-page seed (the intro_e analog). H1: structure tracks anchor.
- **Arm B (steering):** observer agent armed with a **few-shot bank mined from your actual prompts** — the seven templates the record contains: name-the-assumption; scope-audit ("rigorous in differentiating X vs Y?"); predict-then-compare; sample-raw-I/O; simple-but-no-simpler; relate-to-whole; no-solutions-yet. Three sub-arms at matched content: questions / same content as declarative checklist / none. Separates form from content — the thing the record can't.
- **Evaluation, pre-registered before any draft exists:** (1) structural metrics from T3 (inheritance n-grams, jargon density, source-order correlation); (2) you write the known-but-unstated issues of latent_skeptic into a sealed blind key *first*; measure which arms surface them; (3) blind rating of shuffled drafts on three named axes (unfolds / simple-no-simpler / scope-rigor); (4) whatever trace-analog latent_skeptic's artifacts support.
- **Predictions filed now:** H1 — Arm A dominates Arm B; unsteered shape = heuristics-catalogue, not chronicle. H2 — oracle-checkable properties pass everywhere, uncovered ones only in steered arms. Observer crux — question sub-arm beats checklist sub-arm iff form matters; observer questions include ≥1 sealed-key item iff models can generate the naming, not just answer it.

I can mine the few-shot bank and draft the sealed-key protocol whenever you say — the bank is your own prompt vocabulary, which this retro has already indexed.

content.text:
No new tool runs needed — the record already contains what this turn needs; citing from evidence in hand.

## How questions form — what the record actually shows

Every catalytic question in the census traces to one of three geneses:

**Route 1 — expectation violation.** A stated prediction meets a mismatching artifact; the question is automatic ("several movable items moved *against* the push. Quantifying" — 09:47, model, unprompted). Requires a prediction to exist *in writing first*. This is what pre-registration and your "what do we expect and why" template manufacture. All autonomous agent questions in the record are this route. Note: this route only interrogates *within* the frame — it questions the result, never the question.

**Route 2 — juxtaposition.** Two representations sit side by side and misfit: our completions vs Eleos/Berg sources (→ 16:01); claim "both models" vs cell inventory 7-of-8 instruct (→ 11:06); two nulled runs vs a frame still speaking "sycophancy direction" (→ 13:13); goal draft saying "pushback" vs items having no contested fact (→ 15:32). **Every frame-class question is this route, and every one was human.** The human's advantage isn't cleverness — it's that they were actually holding both objects at once. The anchored agent holds one and reads the other through it.

**Route 3 — blocked completion.** "Do not propose solutions until discussed" removes the answer-attractor; what surfaces instead is gaps stated as questions ("two genuine gaps in the data do exist… I'm naming them without proposing anything" — 16:04). Also produced this retro's own open questions, under your no-hypotheses instruction. Cheap, reliable, but note: record shows it eliciting *within-frame* gaps; no evidence yet it elicits frame-naming.

One structural precondition, easy to miss: **frames became questionable only once externalized as a small text object.** 15:32's demolition was possible because 15:28 had written the goal down — the frame became an artifact, attackable like one. Your "restate the hypothesis every turn" norm is a frame-externalization pump. A frame that lives only implicitly in behaviour has no surface for a question to attach to. So "how do questions arise from data" decomposes: data alone → route 1 only, and only against registered expectations. Frame questions need a *pair* — and one member of the pair must be the frame itself, written down small.

Record contains **zero** agent-generated frame-naming questions consumed by anyone. Backtest's job is to find out whether that zero is capability or configuration.

## MECE buckets — my prediction, then yours

Predicted mine before comparing (by mechanism addressed):

- **A. Frame control** (anchor curation, seed texts, specific negations, frame externalization) — targets M1/M2.
- **B. Check coverage** (prose oracles, scope linter, trace analogs, pre-registration extensions) — targets M3.
- **C. Question generation** (observer config, few-shot bank, route-3 elicitation) — targets the human-gate bottleneck.
- **D. Evaluation apparatus** (sealed keys, blind ratings, structural metrics) — meta, tests A–C.

Yours: **question generation** and **write-ups**. Comparison: yours cut by activity, mine by mechanism. Your "question generation" ≈ my C plus most of A — correctly so: a negation's delivery vehicle *is* a question, so frame control collapses into question generation upstream. Your "write-ups" ≈ my A-downstream + B-prose + D-partial. What your two buckets leave uncovered: **B, the oracles** — unless you fold them into write-ups. I'd keep them separate: census says oracle coverage is the single strongest predictor of autonomous correction, and oracles are buildable without solving question generation at all. So: your two buckets + oracles = MECE, and I agree question generation is the upstream one — it *generates* the negations, seeds, and even the oracles (a good question is a check not yet mechanized).

## Your backtest idea, discussed thoroughly

The idea: the record is a labeled dataset. ~15 catalytic prompts, each with a reconstructable before-state and a measured after-state. Ask: can a model, given the before-state, produce the question that worked?

What makes it strong:

1. **Labels exist on both sides.** Not just positives — the record holds *inert* questions too (74% of prompts had questions; most produced no catch). So we can score discrimination, not just generation: does the model rank the working question above plausible duds?
2. **Before-states are mostly mechanical to reconstruct.** The human's before-state was largely the conversation itself — truncate the jsonl at t, include only results-records with `timestamp_utc` < t. No summarization by anything that has seen the after-state — that's the leakage rule, and it's the one place your word "abstract" worries me: an abstraction of the before-state written by someone who knows the answer launders the answer into the abstraction ("state includes: replication claim resting on identical seeds" hands it over). Abstract mechanically or with a pre-t-only model, never post-hoc.
3. **Stratification is already done.** Census gives tiers: pointing-class events (12:06-type — expect high recall, near-inevitable given the data), assumption-naming class (13:13, 15:32, 16:01, 11:06, 23:11 — the real test), and route-1 events (should be recoverable by any model given the registered predictions — a calibration floor).
4. **Two-tier scoring, cheap then real.** Tier 1: generate k questions from before-state; blind judge matches against actual + foils; recall@k per tier. Tier 2 (subset, the true metric): feed the generated question to a fresh agent holding the same before-state — does the *after-state reproduce* (the catch fires, the reframe lands)? Elicitation success measured by effect, not surface similarity. Tier 2 also directly tests M2: does the model demolish as competently for a machine-authored naming as it did for yours?
5. **It tests the observer config before building it.** Vary the generator's vantage: (i) in-frame (full conversation context), (ii) blinded artifacts only ("here is a bunch of numbers"), (iii) juxtaposed pairs (draft beside sources; claim beside coverage table), (iv) route-3 instruction added to each. My predictions, filed now: pointing-class recall high everywhere (>½); naming-class recall near zero for (i); (iii) beats (ii) — juxtaposition, not blindness, is the active ingredient; (iv) raises question *count* everywhere but raises *naming* rate only on top of (iii). If (i) matches (iii), anchoring doesn't constrain question generation and the observer config is unnecessary — that would surprise me and kill part of H1.

Honest limits: n ≈ 15, ~5-6 in the class that matters — existence and ordering results, not rates. Events whose trigger lived outside the transcript (01:44 external feedback, your Obsidian-side realizations) can't be backtested — mark excluded, don't fake them. And one bias to respect: the working questions are *your* idiolect; a semantically-right generated question phrased differently must not lose points — hence tier 2.

Fit with the other candidates: backtest is cheaper and controlled; latent_skeptic post is ecological and forward-looking. Right order is backtest → configure observer from what it shows → forward-test on latent_skeptic (keeping the differential H1 prediction: unsteered latent_skeptic drafts should inherit heuristics-catalogue shape, not chronicle). And your instinct that question generation is easier to test than write-ups is borne out by the design: the write-up test needs you rating shuffled drafts; the backtest's ground truth is already in the transcripts.

Simplest possible pilot, one afternoon-sized, before any harness: **one event, the determinism catch.** Before-state = the four battery records as committed Aug 14, nothing else. Question to beat: "are these runs independent?" It is generateable from the artifacts alone (byte-identical floats are sitting there), it was missed in-frame for two days, and it needs no transcript reconstruction. If no vantage elicits it, the observer idea has a problem; if (iii) elicits it and (i) doesn't, we have the mechanism in a bottle.
